title: @object-ui/core evaluatePlainCondition still reads a bare-string predicate on the legacy JS grammar after #27457
body:
domain:ui#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgXU26UBEjd1KKHgNEx

Filing gate: ② a declared-vs-enforced gap on a published export, found by the contract review of PR #27584 (#27457), record 6499697983 should-fix 3.
Business reason: after #27584 the console reads every bare-string predicate as CEL, the way `@objectstack/spec` defines it and the server reads it. `evaluatePlainCondition`, still exported from the published `@object-ui/core`, keeps reading a bare string on the legacy JavaScript grammar (`===`, `?.`, `.includes(` …), and its own tests pin that. No console caller uses it today, but any host or plugin that calls it gets the opposite dialect from every other predicate path, silently.
Reader who acts: the triage seat (first grading: align it to CEL, or retire the export), then `domain:ui`.
Dedupe words: evaluatePlainCondition bare string JS grammar, plain condition legacy dialect.

## Mechanism

- `ui/packages/core/src/evaluator/` `evaluatePlainCondition` (published export) evaluates a bare string on the legacy grammar; `ExpressionEvaluator.evaluateCondition` routes the same string to CEL after #27584.
- Its tests pin `===`.
- Spec: `packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts` transforms a bare string to `{ dialect: 'cel', source }`.
